feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=2x$ and $f(2)=4.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=2$ to estimate the value of $f(3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(2)=4,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=2x,$ then ${f}^{′}(2)=2(2)=4.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=4+4(x-2).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(3)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & ≈L(3) \\  & =4+4(3-2) \\  & =4+4(1) \\  & =4+4 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
